children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my child, Alex. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about **Alex**.

To assess eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather some details about Alex and your circumstances.

**First, could you tell me: How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Alex is 8 years old.

**Next, could you tell me: Is Alex your biological child, adopted child, or are you their legal guardian in some other way?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is my child, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. 

**Could you tell me: Are you currently living in the UK, and if so, what is your residency status?** (For example, are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status, a visa, etc.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm living in the UK. I live in Bristol.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know you're living in Bristol.

**To continue, could you clarify your residency status in the UK?** For example, are you a British citizen, do you have settled status, a visa, or another type of immigration status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information.

**Now, could you tell me: Are you currently working, and if so, do you receive any income from employment or self-employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I do work, yes. I have a job.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know you're employed.

**Could you tell me: What is your approximate annual income from your job?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not share my exact income if that's okay. Is that needed for Child Benefit eligibility?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a fair question! Actually, **Child Benefit eligibility itself doesn't depend on your income level** — it's available to eligible claimants regardless of how much they earn.

However, there is a separate consideration called the **High Income Child Benefit Charge**, which may affect you if your income is above a certain threshold, but that's a tax matter rather than an eligibility issue for the benefit itself.

So for the purposes of determining your eligibility, I don't need your exact income figure.

**Let me ask instead: Does Alex live with you permanently as part of your household?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

**Could you tell me: Where does Alex live, and what is your arrangement with Alex's other parent or guardian?** For example, do you have regular contact or shared care arrangements with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with their other parent. We're separated, so Alex lives with them full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that situation.

**To help me understand this better: Do you have any financial responsibility for Alex, such as paying child maintenance or support to the other parent?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute financially. I help with their expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**One more question to clarify: Does Alex live in the UK with the other parent?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives in the UK with their other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the details you've provided, let me explain the situation:

Child Benefit requires that the child lives with you as part of your household. In your case, Alex lives full-time with their other parent and does not live with you. While you do contribute financially to Alex's care, this alone does not meet the residency requirement for Child Benefit.

The key eligibility criterion is that the child must live in your home as part of your household. Since Alex doesn't meet this requirement, unfortunately you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for them.

However, the other parent — with whom Alex lives — may be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex if they meet the other eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'm sorry that you're not eligible in this case. If you have any other questions or if your circumstances change in the future, please feel free to get in touch.
